- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, dampening the immediate post-spike forecast.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.4), model frequently underestimates; adjust downward by 1–3% to align with mean reversion toward recent low range.
- Model tends to overfit short-term momentum; for 30-day forecasts, apply a 1–2 day mean reversion filter to smooth out erratic peaks.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 day mean to anchor forecast.
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (±10% from recent 18-day range) unless sentiment strongly supports it; cap forecasts within ±5% of recent 18-day volatility band.
